transcript.text: Bosch WTN85201GB condenser dryer not drying properly anymore, clothes still damp after 2 hrs. any ideas

Please switch off and unplug the tumble dryer first, then allow it to cool down completely before proceeding. Damp laundry usually points to an airflow issue, so let’s start with a simple check of the fluff filter located in the door opening. As this is a condenser model, you may also find a second filter at the bottom, which we will look at later if needed. Please refer to the image shown above for guidance on locating these parts. Once you have checked the main filter, let us know: Was it full of fluff (and is it clean now), is the mesh torn, or was it already clean?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the lint filter is" — The fluff/lint filter sits in the door opening or just inside the rim. Lift it out and clear the fluff after every load. Typical layout — your dryer may differ.]
Checked the door filter. It had fluff and a waxy film on it. I rinsed it under the tap and the water barely went through until I scrubbed it.

Thanks for confirming you have cleaned the lint filter on your Bosch condenser dryer. Please run a normal drying programme using a normal load of laundry. Is the laundry coming out dry now, or still damp?
Haven't run a cycle since cleaning the filter yet. Is there anything else I should check first, or just run it?

Thanks for letting us know you haven’t retested yet. Before we look at anything else, we need to check if the dryer is actually heating up. Please run a cycle and let me know: Partway through a drying programme, is the air and the laundry warm, or completely cold?
Ok. Before I run it, it did get hot inside the drum after about 20 min on earlier cycles, so it does heat. Do you want me to check anything else first?

Thanks for letting us know it is getting warm. Overloading the drum or putting in clothes that weren't spun well in the washer can make drying much slower. Please ensure the drum is no more than about two-thirds full. Was it overloaded or were the clothes very wet going in (and have you changed that), or was it a normal, well-spun load?
It was a normal load, 1200 spin, nothing changed there. Anything else I should check before running it?

Thanks for confirming that. Please switch the dryer off, unplug it and let it cool down first. Behind the flap at the bottom front there's a condenser unit (or a second filter on heat-pump models). Take it out and rinse the fluff off under the tap, then let it drip-dry and refit it. You can see an illustration of this in the app below. Was it clogged with fluff (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the condenser and water tank are" — On a condenser dryer the water container pulls out at the top and the condenser/heat exchanger sits behind a flap at the bottom front — slide it out and rinse it. Condenser/heat-pump dryers only; layout may differ.]
Never cleaned that before. Took it out and the front was matted with lint, but it came clean with the shower head. Refitted now. Should I run a cycle?
Thanks for letting us know you’ve cleaned the condenser. Please run a normal drying programme using a normal load to see if that resolves the issue. Is the laundry coming out dry now, or still damp?
I haven't run it yet, I'll do that now. Anything else I should check while it's running or is that it?

Thanks for confirming that. Please switch the dryer off, unplug it and let it cool down first. Sensor dryers stop when two metal strips inside the drum near the filter detect the laundry is dry. Fabric conditioner can coat these strips, causing the machine to stop too early. Wipe them with a damp cloth and a little vinegar. Were they coated or dirty (and are they clean now), or were they already clean?
Bars were slightly dull, wiped them with vinegar. They're clean now. Anything else, or should I just run a cycle?

Thanks for letting us know you’ve cleaned the sensor strips again. Please go ahead and run a normal drying programme using a normal load of laundry. This will help us see how the machine performs after that adjustment. Is the laundry coming out dry now, or still damp?
